entities.name: Abraham Van Helsing
entities.description: A Dutch doctor, philosopher and scientist from Amsterdam, and Seward's old teacher. He is the first to recognise what is wrong with Lucy and leads the hunt for the Count.

entities.name: Lucy Westenra
entities.description: Mina's lively, much-admired friend, courted by three men in one day. She becomes the Count's first victim in England.

entities.name: Mina Harker
entities.description: Born Wilhelmina Murray, a schoolmistress and Jonathan's fiancee, then wife. She types up and orders the diaries, letters and cuttings that make up the book, and becomes central to tracking the Count.

entities.name: Jonathan Harker
entities.description: A young solicitor from Exeter, sent to Transylvania to settle the Count's purchase of a London house. His journal of his time as a prisoner in Castle Dracula opens the novel.

entities.name: Arthur Holmwood
entities.description: Lucy's fiance, who becomes Lord Godalming when his father dies. His title and money open many doors during the hunt.

entities.name: John Seward
entities.description: A young doctor who runs a lunatic asylum next to Carfax. One of Lucy's suitors; he keeps his diary on a phonograph and studies his patient Renfield.

entities.name: Count Dracula
entities.description: An ancient Transylvanian nobleman and vampire. He buys Carfax, an estate near London, and sails to England in boxes of his native earth, where he preys on Lucy and Mina.

entities.name: Quincey Morris
entities.description: A rich, brave young Texan, another of Lucy's suitors and a loyal friend to Arthur and Seward. He joins the hunt with his Winchester and bowie knife.

entities.name: R. M. Renfield
entities.description: A patient in Seward's asylum who eats flies, spiders and birds to absorb their lives. He senses the Count's coming and calls him "Master".

entities.name: Peter Hawkins
entities.description: Jonathan's employer, a solicitor in Exeter who sends him to Transylvania. A fatherly figure to Jonathan and Mina.

entities.name: Mrs. Westenra
entities.description: Lucy's mother, a widow with a weak heart. Kind but unknowing, she undoes some of Van Helsing's precautions.

entities.name: Petrof Skinsky
entities.description: A trader in Galatz who deals with the Slovaks and is engaged to receive the Count's box from the ship.

entities.name: Sam Bloxam
entities.description: A London carrier who moved some of the Count's earth boxes from Carfax. Seward's inquiries lead to him.

entities.name: Thomas Bilder
entities.description: The keeper of the wolves at the Zoological Gardens, interviewed by a newspaper about Bersicker's escape.

entities.name: Bersicker
entities.description: A grey wolf that escapes from the Zoological Gardens in London on the night the Count attacks Lucy's house.

entities.name: Joseph Smollet
entities.description: A carrier's man living in Walworth who helped move the Count's boxes, and remembers where some of them went.

entities.name: Mr. Swales
entities.description: An elderly Whitby sailor who talks with Mina and Lucy in the churchyard on the cliff, scoffing at the lies on the tombstones.

entities.name: Samuel F. Billington
entities.description: A Whitby solicitor to whom the Count's boxes of earth are consigned when they arrive on the Demeter.

entities.name: Captain Donelson's
entities.description: Captain of the Czarina Catherine, the ship that carries the Count's box from London to Galatz. He reports a strangely fast voyage.

entities.name: Immanuel Hildesheim
entities.description: A shipping agent in Galatz who signed for the Count's box and handed it on to Petrof Skinsky.

entities.name: Mary
entities.description: A servant in the Harkers' house in Exeter, who shows Van Helsing in when he first calls on Mina.

entities.name: Sister Agatha
entities.description: A nun at the hospital in Buda-Pesth who nurses Jonathan through brain fever after his escape, and writes to Mina.

entities.name: Demeter
entities.description: The Russian schooner from Varna that carries the Count to Whitby. It runs aground in a storm with its dead captain lashed to the wheel and no living crew.

entities.name: Enoch
entities.description: Not a character: the biblical Enoch, who "walked with God", to whom Renfield compares himself.

entities.name: Geordie
entities.description: A dead man of Whitby buried under the tombstone Mr. Swales calls "a pack of lies", on whose grave Lucy and Mina like to sit.

entities.name: Joseph
entities.description: Not a character: the name comes from the Hospital of St. Joseph and Ste. Mary in Buda-Pesth, where Jonathan is nursed.

entities.name: Thomas Snelling
entities.description: Joseph Smollet's mate, a carrier's man in Bethnal Green who helped move the Count's boxes but is too drunk to remember anything.

entities.name: Dr. Vincent
entities.description: A doctor at the North Hospital who treats the children bitten on Hampstead Heath by the "bloofer lady".

entities.name: Arminius
entities.description: Van Helsing's friend at Buda-Pesth University, who looks into the history of the Voivode Dracula.

entities.name: Attila
entities.description: Attila the Hun, whose blood the Count boasts runs in his veins.

entities.name: Sir John Paxton
entities.description: Two people share this name in the book: a sailor drowned off Cape Farewell, named on a Whitby gravestone, and the President of the Incorporated Law Society, who sends a representative to Mr. Hawkins's funeral.

entities.name: Patrick Hennessey
entities.description: A doctor who looks after Seward's asylum while Seward is away, and reports on Renfield's attacks on the carriers at Carfax.

entities.name: Rufus Smith
entities.description: An agent at Lloyd's in London who telegraphs Lord Godalming with news of the Czarina Catherine.

entities.name: Shakespeare
entities.description: Not a character: William Shakespeare, quoted by Jonathan and by Renfield.
